import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Every app carries an **ABI**: a JSON description of its surface, generated by
`#[app::logic]` at compile time and embedded in the component as the custom
section `calimero:abi`. It is part of the component's bytes, so it is covered by
the bundle's hash and cannot drift from the code it describes.

The node reads it to dispatch and gate calls (`calimero_app_host::Abi::from_json`);
clients read it to learn the methods, arguments and results.

## The format

```json
{
  "abiVersion": 1,
  "world": "calimero:app@0.5.1",
  "state": {
    "fields": { "bookings": "table", "titles": "unorderedMap", "nextId": "counter" },
    "search": { "bookings": [] },
    "version": 3
  },
  "methods": {
    "book": {
      "kind": "call",
      "params": [["roomId", "string"], ["start", "u64"], ["title", "string"]],
      "returns": "string",
      "confirm": false, "public": false, "allowSystem": false
    },
    "roomCount": {
      "kind": "view",
      "params": [["roomId", "string"]],
      "returns": "u64",
      "confirm": false, "public": true, "allowSystem": false
    },
    "heartbeat": {
      "kind": "timer", "params": [], "returns": "unit",
      "every": "30s", "confirm": false, "public": false, "allowSystem": true
    }
  },
  "errors": { "NotFound": {}, "Taken": { "start": "u64" }, "Invalid": { "0": "string" } },
  "events": { "Booked": { "id": "string", "roomId": "string", "start": "u64" } }
}
```

- **`methods`**, by camelCase name. `kind` is `init`, `call`, `view`, `timer` or
  `action`. `params` are ordered `[name, type]` pairs. The flags come from the
  [method attributes](/core/build/sdk-macros/#method-attributes): `confirm`,
  `public` (and `rate`), `allowSystem`, `every` on timers, `allowApps`,
  `allowAction`.
- **`state`**: each field's kind, the search fields of each table, and the
  `#[app::state(version = N)]`.
- **`errors`** and **`events`**: each code or name with its fields.
- **Types**: Rust integer, float and bool names, `string`, `bytes`,
  `option<T>`, `list<T>`, `tuple<..>`, `unit`, else the Rust type's name.
  `u64`, `i64` and `bytes` are strings on the wire.

Every object's keys are written in sorted order, so the same source always
produces the same bytes.

## What the node enforces

The host reads `abiVersion` (and refuses one it does not support), the method
kinds, and the flags: a view never runs as a write, `confirm` needs a fresh
passkey assertion, `public` admits callers who are not signed in, `allowSystem`,
`allowApps` and `allowAction` admit the node, other apps and the app's own
actions. Free-form keys (`params`, `returns`, `errors`, `events`) describe the
app to clients; nodes ignore them. A field the host enforces is added only with
an `abiVersion` bump.

## Read it

- `GET /apps/{app}/abi` returns an installed app's ABI
  ([Node API](/core/operate/admin-api/)); `meroctl context abi` prints it.
- mero-js and calimero-client-py read it to build typed calls.

<Aside type="note">
  Upgrades compare the state section of the two ABIs: see
  [Upgrades & state](/core/build/migrations/).
</Aside>
